liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Weight** (3 reviews): Attendee lists The Weight as a highlight of the show; Reviewer says the band nailed it, only the second time it had been played [22][27][30]
- **Death Don't Have No Mercy** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls this version spectacular; Reviewer calls this version a plain classic [27][28][29]
- **Easy To Love You** (1 review): Attendee calls Easy To Love You a sweet highlight [22]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Reviewer enjoyed Jerry's delivery of the 'burned like hell' lyric [19]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer describes it as wicked, with a palpable sense of something growing [30]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Reviewer calls this second-set opener one of the best versions they've heard, crisp and clean [19]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Attendee's highlight; Bobby had a rock-god presence, the crowd went wild, and the tape captures the thunder [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-04-02.nak.cohen.106763.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 138 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1990-04-02.mtx.hansokolow.97216.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 142 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: One very minor digital spot at 3:16 in Space, otherwise flawless [2]
- **gd1990-04-02.154440.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 142 min [3]
- **gd90-04-02.nak.nawrocki.3299.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 18 songs; 146 min; rated 3.6/5 by 10 [9]. Said about its sound: This download has crisp sound and a full presence [30]
- **gd90-04-02.sbd.dodd.17731.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 140 min; rated 4.27/5 by 21 [16]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds crisp and clean, with wonderful transitions throughout the show; Track 1 on this soundboard is crowd noise and tuning, so every track number is off by one; Sound quality is great, though the vocals show some strain [19][21][28]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended all three Atlanta nights, tickets bought for them at $18.50 each while they were in treatment [24]
- The crowd was heavily into the first set [26]
- A very large train passed by the parking lot, which the reviewer found hilarious [27]
- It was the reviewer's first show, and its emotional intensity struck them, with the whole band present [29]
- Says the Looks Like Rain on Without a Net is from 28 March 1990 at Nassau Coliseum, not this show [23]
- Notes the run's other shows: Eyes with Branford Marsalis on 29 March 1990, Help>Slipknot>Franklin's on 30 March [23]
- Says the first night opened with Touch of Grey, and this second night was their favorite [24]
- Reviewer judges this the best Omni show of the run [26]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-04-02.nak.cohen.106763.flac16**: taped by Dave Cohen; transferred by Dave Cohen; source: 2 Nakamichi CM300s/ CP4's w/1 Nakamichi CM300/CP2> Nakamichi 550 w/Maxell XLIIS90 cassette masters. Dolby B was used on the Master Cassettes. OTS 8 foot stand… [1]
- **gd1990-04-02.mtx.hansokolow.97216.flac16**: transferred by hansokolow; source: matrix of SBD: shnid=17731 and AUD: shnid=3299 by hansokolow using ProTools [2]. Also: Matrix made by hansokolow in ProTools, an upgrade using the master soundboard cassette; an earlier seed had hiss suggesting later generation; Audience source chain: Nak 300s with CP4s into a Marantz PMD420 analog deck, DAT, CDR; shn by Doug Nawrocki [2]
- **gd1990-04-02.154440.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 16, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X) [3]. Also: This is an UltraMatrix conversion of the 24-bit/96k release 152287 down to 16-bit/44.1k [3]
- **gd90-04-02.nak.nawrocki.3299.sbeok.shnf**: source: Nak 300's/cp 4's > *Marantz PMD420 (mc) > dat > cdr >eac (range extracted at 100% for retracking) > cdwave > mkwact [9]
- **gd90-04-02.sbd.dodd.17731.sbeok.shnf**: source: MSC> DAT> Cdr > Eac > cool edit pro > cdwav > shntool > shnv3 [16]
